Title: Ex-pilot with drug record, foreign woman identified in Laos private jet drug trafficking probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police have identified two Filipinos, including a former pilot, believed to be involved in an international drug trafficking syndicate linked to the seizure of more than half a tonne of methamphetamine aboard a private jet in Laos.
Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations revealed that the former pilot had chartered the aircraft through a Malaysian broker, while other suspect, a woman, was believed to have acted as the syndicate's coordinator.
The former pilot, 54, has a drug-related criminal record, while the woman is 51.
Hussein said the latest findings followed investigations into the seizure at Luang Prabang International Airport in Laos, which also led to the detention of a Malaysian pilot.

Title: Malaysia, China to step up cooperation against cyber scams, drug smuggling
Article:
BEIJING: Cross-border investigations and the recovery of assets stolen through cyber scams are among Malaysia's key priorities in strengthening security cooperation with China, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said closer bilateral cooperation would help both countries tackle transnational crime while delivering practical benefits under their comprehensive strategic partnership, particularly in security and law enforcement.
"We face several challenges in dealing with cyber scams, as the victims are not limited to Chinese nationals.
"That is why I believe bilateral cooperation between our countries is crucial in addressing this problem," he told Malaysian media at a press conference here today.
Zahid is on a five -day working visit to Beijing and Tianjin, which began yesterday.
He said Malaysia and China were also strengthening intelligence sharing and coordinating investigations and enforcement operations to combat cross-border crime.
Both countries had established a joint security committee, which also focuses on combating drug smuggling.
"Besides intelligence sharing and enforcement, we are adopting new methods to obtain early information on drug smuggling operations and facilities used to process illicit drugs.
"These efforts are already under way and will be further strengthened," he said, adding that cooperation between the police and China's National Narcotics Control Commission remained close.
Zahid said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had held several discussions with his Chinese counterpart on the matter.
He said Malaysia, through the Drug Prevention Committee, which he chairs, recognised the importance of cross-border cooperation, with both countries making progress in their efforts.
On cyber scams, Zahid said Malaysia joined a programme under the International Alliance Against Telecommunications and Cyber Fraud on Sept 10, with cross-border investigations and the recovery of stolen assets identified as priorities.
"To strengthen the legal framework against cybercrime, I personally tabled the Cybercrime Bill in the Dewan Rakyat during the parliamentary sitting last July," he said.

Title: 492 foreign workers detained in Johor factory raid
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Some 492 foreign workers were detained and a factory manager arrested during an immigration raid at an automotive and electronics components factory in Tebrau, Johor.
The manager was arrested for allegedly harbouring migrants.
The joint operation by the Johor Immigration Department and the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) began at 10am and ended at 12.30pm yesterday.
Johor Immigration director Datuk Mohd Rusdi Mohd Darus said the authorities had received a tip-off that the factory had allegedly hired migrants to keep operating costs low.
"We mounted surveillance for several weeks before storming the factory.
"Some workers tried to flee and hide but were caught," he said in a statement today.
The detainees, aged between 19 and 46, comprised nationals from Myanmar, Bangladesh, Nepal, India, Pakistan, Indonesia and Cambodia.
They were suspected of committing immigration offences, including working without valid authorisation or failing to produce valid documents.
All 492 detainees were taken to the Setia Tropika Immigration Depot.

Title: BYD expands Sarawak network with Miri 3S centre
Article:
BYD Sime Motors has opened a new 3S centre in Miri, Sarawak, expanding its sales and aftersales network in the state as it builds up support for its electric vehicles (EVs).
The 12,228 square feet (sq ft) facility is the company's largest 3S centre in Sarawak, combining vehicle sales, servicing and spare parts under one roof.
It comprises a 5,838 sq ft showroom with space for five vehicles and a 6,390 sq ft service centre equipped with six service bays, with capacity to handle up to 35 vehicles daily.
Other facilities include a customer lounge, vehicle delivery bay and EV charging points for sales and service customers.
The centre is operated by Kah Progression Auto Sdn Bhd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Oriental Holdings Bhd, and has 15 employees across its sales and aftersales operations.
Sime Motors Southeast Asia managing director Jeffrey Gan said the facility would increase the group's capacity to serve customers in Sarawak.
The opening follows Sime Motors' establishment of East Malaysia's first BYD 3S centre in Kota Kinabalu in December 2024.
BYD Sime Motors now has three authorised outlets in Sarawak, located in Kuching, Sibu and Miri, with the latest facility providing additional service capacity for customers in the northern part of the state.
BYD Malaysia managing director Jacob Ma said the expansion was aimed at making the company's vehicles and aftersales services more accessible as EV adoption spreads beyond major cities.
"The opening of the Miri 3S Ccentre marks another important step in strengthening BYD's presence in East Malaysia.
"As EV adoption grows beyond major cities, we want to be closer to our customers and make our products and aftersales support more accessible," Ma added.
To mark the opening, Kah Progression Auto will hold a roadshow at Bintang Megamall's Ground Floor, East Court (Old Wing), from Oct 16-18.

Title: Kelantan prepares 451 evacuation centres ahead of monsoon
Article:
KOTA BARU: Kelantan has prepared 451 temporary evacuation centres (PPS) with the capacity to accommodate 200,000 flood victims ahead of the coming northeast monsoon.
State Social Welfare Department director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said the centres were located across all districts, with most in Pasir Mas and Tumpat.
He said 162 forward bases had also been set up as part of the state's flood preparedness measures.
"All agencies involved are ready to face any eventuality, as floods could hit the state at any time.
"All food supplies and other essential equipment have been delivered to the 162 forward bases across all districts.
"The distribution was completed last month," he said to reporters after officiating the 2026 Temporary Evacuation Centre Management Training and Simulation Programme.
He said the annual exercise was aimed at refreshing the knowledge and skills of personnel from government agencies involved in flood disaster management.
The exercise also involved community representatives, including penggawa (local administrative heads), to ensure effective coordination and preparedness during emergencies.
"A total of 249 participants took part in today's exercise for Kota Baru district," he said.
Che Samsuzuki said 12 similar programmes would be held statewide, with the series beginning in early October.
He said the exercises were important to ensure all parties remained prepared and up to date on procedures and challenges in disaster management, particularly during floods.

Title: Maybank lawsuit reinstated: Court orders trial over unauthorised RM60k transfer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man who claimed that nearly RM60,000 disappeared from his Maybank account in just eight minutes has won his appeal to reinstate his lawsuit against the bank.
The Johor Baru High Court ruled that Wong Bair Lim's allegations of negligence and unauthorised online transfers raised issues that could only be resolved through a full trial.
Judicial commissioner Noradura Hamzah said the Sessions Court had erred in dismissing Wong's lawsuit without properly examining the disputed facts.
These included whether Wong had authorised the transactions and whether the bank had taken adequate steps to prevent possible fraud.
"The Sessions Court erred when it made findings of fact and resolved disputed issues at the striking-out stage.
"This was contrary to the established principle that a court should not conduct a detailed examination of documents and facts at such a stage," she said in her grounds of judgment published by the Judiciary Department today.
The case stemmed from an incident on July 13, 2024, when Wong discovered that RM59,867.61 had been transferred from his savings account through Maybank2u.
The money was transferred to four unknown recipients through 5 transactions carried out between 1.44pm and 1.52pm.
Just two minutes before the transfers began, the daily transaction limit on Wong's account had been increased from RM2,000 to RM60,000.
Wong lodged a police report on the same day before filing a lawsuit against Maybank in October 2024.
He alleged that the bank had failed to prevent the unauthorised transfers and had not taken appropriate action after receiving his complaint.
Maybank maintained that the transactions had been carried out and approved through Wong's registered device.
The bank also argued that Wong had downloaded a third-party application, which it said had contributed to his losses.
On Nov 14 last year, the Sessions Court allowed Maybank's application to strike out Wong's lawsuit, finding that his claim was frivolous, vexatious and unsustainable.
However, Noradura ruled that the lower court had made findings on disputed facts that should have been determined at a full trial.
Among the questions requiring examination were whether Wong had personally approved the transactions, who had increased his daily transfer limit and whether the bank's security verification system had been accessed by an unauthorised party.
Noradura also said banks had a duty to exercise reasonable care when carrying out customers' payment instructions, particularly in cases involving possible online fraud.
She said whether Maybank owed Wong a duty of care in the circumstances and whether that duty had been breached could not be determined without a full trial.
"The defendant's duty of care after receiving a complaint about unauthorised transfers is an issue that requires an assessment of the facts at a full trial.
"This issue alone is sufficient to prevent the plaintiff's action from being struck out summarily," she said.
She ordered the case, including pending applications, to be returned to the Johor Baru Sessions Court for further proceedings and a full trial.
Maybank was also ordered to pay Wong RM8,000 in appeal costs, subject to allocatur, before the trial begins.
The High Court's decision does not determine whether Maybank was responsible for Wong's losses, as that question remains to be decided at trial.
Wong was represented by Lim Pang Kiat and Fung Yu Qi, while Maybank was represented by Tengku Nazihah Hanis Tengku Abd Nawawi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Onn Hafiz: Johor's 8pc growth no reason for complacency
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor must turn its strong economic growth and investment inflows into high-paying jobs for locals and greater opportunities for small businesses, said Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
He said the state's economy grew by eight per cent last year, the highest in the country, but the achievement should not breed complacency.
"If we want extraordinary results, our thinking and the way we work must also be extraordinary," he said in his speech at the "Towards a Futuristic Nation: Leadership, Innovation and Transformation" forum.
It was held in conjunction with the International Young Future Leaders Summit (iFUTURE) 2026, held at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
The forum also featured Umno leader Khairy Jamaluddin and Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, with more than 1,200 student leaders from Malaysia and 53 other countries attending the summit.
Onn Hafiz said investments, particularly through the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), must create more high-income employment for locals, help small and medium enterprises expand and ensure balanced and sustainable development.
He said that leadership required integrity, fairness and sincerity, adding that leaders must lead by example and ensure policies deliver tangible benefits to the people.
"Young people must not merely be spectators to change, but seize the opportunities created by the state's rapid development," he said, encouraging them to equip themselves with knowledge and skills and prepare to lead in the future.
He said developing Johor's youth remained a key priority under the Maju Johor 2030 agenda.

Title: The guest that came early and we don't really know what to do
Article:
IN September 2026, something pivotal happened to the Malaysian automotive landscape: the total number of battery electric vehicles cracked the 10 per cent mark, at least a year ahead of most optimistic predictions.
The writing was on the wall. Proton New Energy Technology, or Pro-Net - the subsidiary entrusted to explore the electrified market for the nation's oldest carmaker - reported achieving 20,000 total unit sales sometime in June.
Not three months later, they sent out invitations to the media to mark the 40,000th delivery of their e.Mas brand, a doubling that took a mere three months.
This was made possible by the staggering response of the buying public to the e.Mas 5 electric hatchback.
This cheerful little car has been regularly clearing 4,000 units every month for the past few months.
If you have no idea that there is a substantial chunk of LFP under the floor, you might think that Proton has just found another best-seller, regardless of motors or magnets.
And so, in September, BEV sales hit 11 per cent. For anyone watching the transition, it is almost certain that we have entered the inflection zone - that spot between 10 and 15 per cent where most technology starts to take root and rapidly begins to dominate the market.
If you had asked me three years ago when we would hit the inflection point, I would have carefully hazarded a guess that it would likely be in 2027, and if we stumbled a bit, it would be 2028, but definitely before 2030.
There is a rather obvious logic to the inflection point.
Just because something is a new technology, it doesn't mean that it will replace the old, because some technologies are not really useful.
These sorts of technologies linger on for a while and die; sometimes, their carcasses will encourage the growth of a much more useful successor.
Case in point: the electronic diary. When it came out in the early 1990s, it never really took off because writing in a paper diary or, if you were a yuppie, a Filofax, was certainly easier.
That died a slow death sometime in the late 1990s, leaving behind names like Apple's Newton, the PalmPilot, and Psion.
I was a cheapskate and bought an entry-level Casio digital diary.
This death coincided with developments in cellular radio transmission technology that gave us fantastic bandwidth and birthed the smartphone we carry today.
Well, the diary is a key component of the smartphone - just two rungs under some game and social media stuff - but you get the idea.
The digital diary never crossed the 10 percent mark, so it died.
The motorcar did, and it made horses unemployed. The telephone did, and fired all telegraph operators.
The washing machine crossed the Rubicon and made washing maidsobsolete.
Radio, television, aeroplanes, computers, and the internet all made it after crossing the turning point.
In fact, of all the things listed here, the motorcar took the longest to become a mass-market sensation, hitting the inflection point sometime in 1915 and only becoming the dominant form of personal transportation sometime in the 1960s.
It was slowed down by World War I and World War II.
This time around, the world has hit around 22 per cent TIV for fully electric vehicles.
If you combine that number with Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles, they form the majority of global vehicle sales, pushing ICE into the minority for the first time this September as well.
It's not a coincidence; it is the obvious trend. What this means is that the age of electric land transportation has come of age, and as with any idea whose time has come, no one can stop it.
From this month onwards, we will continue to monitor BEV and PHEV sales in Malaysia, and it would be odd to see the curve suddenly dip south.
Right now, we have 131,000 BEVs on the road. This likely means that nearly every other housing estate has one, spreading the virus locally.
While I am pleased that EV sales have exceeded even my lofty expectations, it is concerning that the charging network is trailing behind.
I am also concerned for the Malaysian automotive industry as a whole because we are, frankly, not prepared for this unexpected turn of events - not least when it comes to localising key components.
Although I have not had a chance to interrogate the successful people at Pro-Net, I am quite willing to bet that they don't have a plan on how to localise batteries, traction motors, or the Battery Management Software, never mind the rest.
One of the reasons why they are not ready is because they were not expecting this success.
How do I know this? Because Proton's EV factory was opened with a capacity of producing 20,000 cars a year, and they hit that number in three months.
I know that they are really struggling to wrap their heads around this because, when they launched the factory, they told us that they would double the capacity to 40,000 units by the end of 2026.
Well, even if they manage to increase capacity in record time this month, they are still going to be behind by about 30 per cent.
Realistically, they should upgrade their EV plant to 100,000 units so that they can handle growth for the next five years.
That's how unexpected this sudden rise in EV volume has been for everyone.
To be sure, the main concern is that almost all EVs sold in this country, regardless of badge, come from China, and they have a terrifying grip on the supply chain and battery technology with no real competition from Japan, Europe, or the United States.
We are fast coming up against a huge monopoly, and we need some strong and steady hands to steer this ship.
China has a habit of ramping up their presence in a way that seems rude because they do it so thoroughly.
Chinese brands don't just bring cars; when they do local assembly, they bring their own suppliers, their own dealerships, and sometimes even the people who work in the dealerships.
This leaves very little for the real local Malaysian players.
So yes, I am glad that EVs are taking off, but I am very concerned that we may not have a handle on this matter right now.
Tell me I'm wrong. Please
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Veterans who retired before 2013 still awaiting pension adjustments – Ketereh MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Veterans who retired before Jan 1, 2013, are still awaiting pension adjustments, leaving them receiving lower pensions than those who retired after that date, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Datuk Khlir Mohd Nor (PN-Ketereh) said the disparity remained unresolved despite repeated appeals.
He called on the Defence Ministry (Mindef) to provide a list of surviving veterans who retired before Jan 1, 2013, and disclose the cost of adjusting their pensions.
"I request Mindef to submit the list of veterans who retired before January 1, 2013, who are still around, and how much money is needed to resolve this pension adjustment," he said during the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat.
Khlir said many of the affected veterans had served between 1946 and 1990 and were now aged 60 and above.
"The majority of veterans who retired before January 1, 2013 are personnel who served during the emergency era, which is from 1946 to 1990, where their average age today is 60 years and above," he said.
Khlir said the eight per cent increase under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), which took effect on Dec 1, 2024, was welcomed, but the pension disparity still needed to be addressed.
He added that the number of affected veterans had declined as many had died while waiting for their pensions to be adjusted.
"Now, out of that 78,000 (veterans who retired before 2013), I think there are only 40,000 left. The others have died. So they don't get to experience it," he said.
Citing data from the Armed Forces Veterans Affairs Department (JHEV), Khlir said there were 221,312 Armed Forces veterans nationwide as of July 30, 2025,, with about 6,000 more expected to join their ranks annually.
He said most veterans served for 21 years due to the nature of military service, while 93.24 per cent received pensions equivalent to 50 per cent of their final salaries, having fallen short of the 25 years and three months of service required to qualify for a pension equivalent to 60 per cent of their final salaries.
Khlir, himself a veteran, called for the issue to be resolved under Section 187 of the Armed Forces Act 1972.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze forces school closures in 3 Pahang districts
Article:
KUANTAN: Pekan will be the third district in Pahang, after Kuantan and Rompin, to close schools tomorrow due to worsening haze, the Pahang Education Department said.
In a statement, the department said all educational institutions under its jurisdiction in the three districts would be closed, with Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) conducted.
"The department prioritises the safety, health and well-being of students and teachers amid the current haze situation," it said.
The department said the Sijil Tinggi Agama Malaysia (STAM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) examinations would proceed as scheduled.
The examinations would be conducted in compliance with the prevailing standard operating procedures and safety measures, the statement said.
Candidates and examination personnel were advised to refer to further announcements and instructions from their schools, examination centres and the department's official channels.
The department urged parents to ensure that students attending lessons or sitting examinations wore face masks.
As of 5pm, two air quality monitoring stations in Pahang had recorded unhealthy readings, with Balok Baru in Kuantan registering an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 159 and Rompin recording 157.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian busted trying to smuggle 980 cigarette packs into Singapore
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A Malaysian man's attempt to enter Singapore with duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden in his pickup truck's tyres came unstuck at Woodlands Checkpoint, where officers uncovered more than 980 boxes.
The 31-year-old was arrested after Singapore Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officers diverted his Malaysia-registered car for enhanced checks on Sept 26.
ICA said its search and examination officers discovered the cigarettes concealed within the tyres. Photographs shared by ICA showed that the tyres had been cut open and stuffed with cigarette boxes in an attempt to evade detection.
The man, along with the seized items, was referred to Singapore Customs for further investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit ends marginally lower against US dollar ahead of US inflation data
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed slightly lower against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the United States inflation data due tomorrow, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the ringgit eased to 4.0835/0880 against the greenback from Monday's close of 4.0820/0865.
TA Securities chief economist Shazma Juliana Abu Bakar said the data could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's monetary policy direction and, consequently, near-term movements in the ringgit.
However, she said the ringgit is expected to remain relatively resilient throughout this week, supported by positive investor sentiment following the 2027 Budget and the government's continued commitment to fiscal consolidation.
"Yet, escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia and elevated Brent crude oil prices could heighten external uncertainties and sustain demand for the US dollar as a safe-haven currency," she told Bernama.
At the close, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.
The local note was lower against the Japanese yen to 2.5833/5864 from 2.5739/5769 at Monday's close, inched down against the British pound to 5.4057/4177 from 5.4017/4077 and eased against the euro to 4.5654/5704 from 4.5637/5687.
Against its Asean peers, the local note decreased against the Indonesian rupiah to 228.1/228.4 from 227.9/228.2, but remained unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.50/6.51.
It edged down against the Singapore dollar to 3.1902/1940 from 3.1873/1911 at Monday's close and slid against the Thai baht to 12.1663/1844from 12.1391/1568.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lianson Fleet buys US$23mil bulk carrier
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lianson Fleet Group Bhd has bought a Japanese-built bulk carrier for US$23 million or about RM93.9 million.
This is part of Lianson Fleet's strategy to expand its marine transportation fleet and diversify beyond offshore support vessels.
The vessel, named LFG Cengal, was acquired by its wholly-owned LFG Cengal Ltd from an unrelated third party on Oct 13, the company said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
Built in May 2013, the Ultramax bulk carrier has a deadweight tonnage of 61,446 tonnes and is equipped with five cargo holds and five cargo hatches.
"The vessel acquisition is funded through internally generated funds," it added.
The vessel is expected to contribute positively to earnings through charter income for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 and beyond.
The company said the acquisition would strengthen its recurring income stream and improve earnings visibility, supported by the vessel's long-term charter potential and utilisation.
"Demand and charter rates for bulk carriers remain robust, supported by regional trade flows of bulk cargo and commodities.
"Elevated tonne-miles are also observed, driven by cargo being rerouted over longer distances due to trade dislocations and regional supply-demand imbalances," it said.
Lianson Fleet said the acquisition is expected to improve earnings visibility by capitalising on prevailing strong charter rates and high utilisation levels for similar vessels.
Managing director Lim Chern Wool said the acquisition supports its strategy to build a diversified maritime business with the scale and capabilities to tap opportunities across the wider industry and sustain growth amid changes in the global maritime landscape.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dewan Rakyat: Pasir Mas, Jelutong MPs clash over Rohingya issue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A heated exchange erupted between government and opposition members of parliament over the Rohingya refugee issue during the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat today.
The argument broke out while Ahmad Fadhli Shaari (PN-Pasir Mas) was debating the budget, when RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) interjected and claimed that Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang (PN-Marang) and former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak had previously welcomed Rohingya refugees into Malaysia.
"Bachok, relax. Bachok, listen. If you dare, listen," Rayer told Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman (PN-Bachok), who tried to interject during the exchange.
"It was not the Tambun MP (Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) who invited refugees from Myanmar to come here. It was Marang and Pekan (Najib)," Rayer said.
Fadhli hit back by citing an April 26, 2020 news report in which Anwar had defended humanitarian assistance for Rohingya refugees.
"I expected Jelutong to raise this. I brought an excerpt dated April 26, 2020.
"Who said this? Anwar. Which Anwar? The Tambun MP," he said.
Rayer maintained that providing humanitarian assistance to refugees was different from encouraging their arrival, arguing that Malaysia could uphold humanitarian principles while pursuing efforts to repatriate them.
Resuming his debate, Fadhli called on the government to take tougher action against refugees who broke the law.
He also proposed establishing controlled refugee settlements, similar to those previously used on Pulau Bidong, to better manage the refugee population.
"If we cannot accommodate 200,000 people, we can study capacities of 10,000 or 20,000," he said, calling for a feasibility and cost study.
Fadhli said Malaysians were increasingly concerned about the continued arrival of refugees, although he acknowledged the humanitarian considerations involved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Stingy newlywed': Syed Saddiq teased during Budget debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Newlywed Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) was the subject of light-hearted teasing in the Dewan Rakyat today, just three days after marrying singer-actress Bella Astillah.
Mohd Sany Hamzan (PH-Hulu Langat) jokingly called him a "pengantin kedekut" (stingy newlywed) when Syed Saddiq appeared reluctant to give way to an interjection during the 2027 Budget debate.
The exchange took place as the former youth and sports minister was highlighting the impact of transboundary haze on schoolchildren, particularly those from low-income families.
"Sorry, I still have a lot more to say," Syed Saddiq told Sany as he sought to continue his speech.
"Stingy newlywed!" Sany quipped in response.
Syed Saddiq apologised and asked to finish his remarks on the haze before allowing further interruptions.
The 33-year-old married Bella,
32, on Saturday in a ceremony at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen admits hitting grandmother with belt, threatening her with parang
Article:
BATU PAHAT: An 18-year-old scrap metal collector pleaded guilty at the Yong Peng magistrate's court today to assaulting his 75-year-old grandmother with a belt and threatening her with a parang.
Khairul Adam Yusof entered the plea after the two charges were read out before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
He was charged under Section 323 of the Penal Code with voluntarily causing hurt to his grandmother at a house along Jalan Labis-Yong Peng at 6pm on Oct 6.
The offence carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
The second charge was under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation by pointing a parang at his grandmother.
Both offences allegedly took place at the same time and location.
According to the facts of the case, Khairul had pressured his grandmother to seek a loan from a neighbour to cover his expenses. When she refused, he became angry and an argument broke out.
He then struck her left shoulder and back with a belt before threatening her with the parang.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while Khairul was represented by National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Tan Song Yan.
The defence applied for a social report from the Social Welfare Department, citing Khairul's status as a young offender. The court allowed the application and set bail at RM5,000 for both charges.
Khairul was unable to pay the bail.
The case was fixed for mention on Nov 24, pending the social report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jati Tinggi banks on RM1.1bil orderbook amid share price weakness
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Jati Tinggi Group Bhd remains confident in its business outlook, citing an outstanding orderbook of about RM1.1 billion despite recent weakness in its share price amid volatility in technology and data centre-related stocks.
The power infrastructure engineering group said there had been no material changes to its business operations or ongoing project execution arising from the recent market volatility.
It attributed the broader market uncertainty partly to concerns over global artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments and financing requirements.
This has weighed on sentiment towards technology and data centre-related companies.
Jati Tinggi shares plunged as much as 29 per cent in early trading today, after more than doubling in value since the start of the year.
The stock opened unchanged at RM1.40 before edging up to RM1.41. By 10am, it had tumbled to RM1.00, approaching the limit-down level of 98 sen.
The sharp decline also triggered a suspension of intraday short selling in the counter.
However, the shares pared their losses to close 7.14 per cent, or 10 sen, lower at RM1.30, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM575.81 million.
Jati Tinggi said its orderbook provides earnings visibility over the next three years, supporting its focus on project delivery and business growth.
The group operates in the power infrastructure engineering sector, undertaking underground cable installation, overhead transmission line construction, substation works and other related electrical infrastructure projects.
Malaysia's power infrastructure sector is expected to benefit from continued investment in grid expansion and modernisation, as well as rising electricity demand from data centres, industrial developments and renewable energy integration.
Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) has allocated RM42.8 billion in capital expenditure under Regulatory Period 4 (RP4), providing a major investment backdrop for the country's electricity supply infrastructure.
The expansion of data centres and other energy-intensive industries is increasing the need for reliable electricity supply, grid capacity and supporting transmission and distribution infrastructure.
The integration of renewable energy sources into the national grid is also creating demand for infrastructure upgrades and related engineering works.
Against this backdrop, Jati Tinggi said it would remain focused on executing existing projects on schedule and strengthening its capabilities to capture opportunities arising from Malaysia's ongoing power infrastructure development.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man jailed 30 years, handed 15 strokes for sexually assaulting daughter
Article:
MUAR: An unemployed man was sentenced to 30 years in prison and 15 strokes of the rotan after pleading guilty to three charges of sexually assaulting his 14-year-old daughter.
Sessions Court judge Emelia Kaswati Mohamad Khalid handed down the sentence today, citing the seriousness of the offences, which took place on separate occasions between Oct 3 and 5 at a house in a settlement in Segamat.
The judge said the victim had been subjected to force and threats, leaving her with no choice but to comply with the accused's demands.
"The interests of the accused cannot outweigh those of the public," she said, adding that similar offences remained prevalent despite heavy sentences imposed by courts nationwide.
The man was charged under Section 14(b), read together with Section 16 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
The case came to light after police received a report on Oct 6, following the girl's reluctance to return to the house where she lived with her father and stepmother.
According to the facts of the case, the girl disclosed the abuse to her stepmother, who then informed the girl's biological mother. They then lodged a police report.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Ameerah Allaudeen prosecuted, while the accused was unrepresented.
The court also ordered the man to undergo counselling during his prison term and placed him under police supervision for three years after completing his sentence.

Title: Tokyo cocaine smuggling bust: Malaysia seeking info from Japanese authorities
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: The Home Ministry is seeking further information from Japanese authorities following the detention of five Malaysians suspected of attempting to smuggle about five kilogrammes of cocaine into Tokyo.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said accurate information was needed to establish the facts surrounding the incident, including how the group allegedly passed security checks at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) before being detained in Japan.
He said he had instructed Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan to contact Japanese authorities to obtain more information.
"The same approach was taken in the case involving the detention of a Malaysian co-pilot in Jakarta last month, which was linked to drugs transported on a private aircraft chartered from Malaysia. However, the drugs in that case did not originate from Malaysia but from Laos.
"Once I receive complete information, I will provide the media with the latest developments," he told reporters after attending a 'Madani Town Hall session with the Home Minister' event at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Merbok here.
Yesterday, media reports said four men and a woman, all Malaysians, were detained at Tokyo's Haneda Airport last Saturday on suspicion of attempting to smuggle about five kilogrammes of cocaine worth 120 million yen (RM3.1 million).
The group is believed to have brought the
drugs from KLIA
before their activities were uncovered during customs inspections upon arrival in Japan.
A Fuji News Network (FNN) report said the operation was detected after customs officers became suspicious of one of the suspects wearing shoes with unusually thick soles.
Initial inspections uncovered cocaine concealed beneath the insoles of two suspects' shoes, before customs officers identified three others believed to have been travelling with them.
A Nippon News Network (NNN) article said three of them had also concealed cocaine using the same method.
Saifuddin said the incident did not mean that the implementation of 17 recommendations or initiatives introduced through a joint committee between the ministry and the Transport Ministry to strengthen airport security controls would be halted.
He said the initiatives were being implemented in three phases, including comprehensive screening of passengers and baggage for destinations identified as high-risk areas or hotspots.
"These hotspot destinations will be subject to 100 per cent screening, including pat-down searches from head to toe, as well as baggage inspections.
"Tokyo was not included in our original list of hotspots. I believe the narcotics division will provide an immediate report on the circumstances surrounding this incident," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RedPlanet IPO oversubscribed 85 times
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RedPlanet Bhd's initial public offering (IPO) has been oversubscribed 85.28 times by the public ahead of its transfer listing from Bursa Malaysia's LEAP Market to the ACE Market on Oct 22.
The enterprise information and communications technology solutions provider said it received 7,031 applications for 1.77 billion issue shares worth RM336.72 million from the public.
The IPO involves issuing 70 million new shares and offering 10 million existing shares for sale through private placement to selected investors.
RedPlanet said the 19.71 million shares reserved for eligible directors, employees and other qualifying persons had been fully subscribed after applying the relevant clawback and reallocation provisions.
The private placement tranches were also fully placed.
It comprised 11.53 million new shares for selected investors, 18.22 million new shares for Bumiputera investors approved by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry, and 10 million existing shares for selected investors.
Managing director Lian Wah Seng said the strong response reflected investor confidence in the group's business fundamentals, technical capabilities and long-term growth prospects.
Lian said the listing transfer will help strengthen the company's market visibility, broaden its investor base and support its next phase of growth.
UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd is the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter and placement agent for the IPO and transfer listing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MEF warns RM3,100 minimum wage could hurt small businesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed RM3,100 minimum wage could discourage entry-level hiring and burden small businesses, the Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) said.
MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said wage decisions must be evidence-based and economically sustainable.
He was responding to the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC), which said the government's newly announced RM2,000 minimum wage was insufficient compared with its RM3,100 demand.
MTUC secretary-general Kamarul Baharin Mansor said the rate fell short of union targets and the RM3,400 living wage paid by government-linked companies and government-linked investment companies.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 when tabling 2027 Budget. The new rate takes effect in June 2027 and is expected to benefit more than four million workers.
Syed Hussain said wage proposals must account for differences in employers' ability to absorb higher costs, particularly among micro, small and medium enterprises.
"What a large corporation can absorb may severely burden a small manufacturer, neighbourhood retailer, family business, small contractor, or thin-margin service provider," he told the New Straits Times.
He said smaller businesses faced higher relative operating costs, tighter financing and weaker bargaining power with suppliers, leaving them less able to absorb sudden increases in payroll costs or invest in automation.
Syed Hussain also cautioned against treating living wage estimates as mandatory minimums across all sectors.
"A living wage estimate is useful for assessing household needs, but imposing it across all sectors without examining regional variations and economic impacts is impractical," he said.
He said wage growth should reflect productivity, job complexity and skills, adding that starting salaries for fresh graduates and semi-skilled workers must align with job value and business performance.
A blanket wage requirement, he said, could distort salary structures and discourage employers from hiring entry-level workers.
Williams Business Consultancy Sdn Bhd founder and director Dr Geoffrey Williams said requiring employers to pay a RM3,100 minimum wage was politically impossible, but achieving that take-home income through government cash top-ups was realistic.
He said the proposed rate would be unviable for many employers, but combining statutory minimum wages with assistance such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah could help bridge the gap.
"This gives firms time to adjust while government top-ups bring workers closer to RM3,100. It won't trigger inflation and will boost local economic spending," he said.
Williams also disputed the argument that wage increases must be matched by productivity gains.
"Wages in Malaysia reflect bargaining power, not productivity. If productivity rises, employers simply keep higher profits instead of paying workers more."

Title: Lorry driver in 12-vehicle crash pleads not guilty to drug-impaired driving
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A 51-year-old lorry driver pleaded not guilty to driving under the influence of drugs, driving against traffic, and injuring four people on Oct 9.
C. Agilan was charged under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum jail term of 10 years and a fine of up to RM50,000 upon conviction.
He is accused of driving a lorry under the influence of methamphetamine and amphetamine at about 4.30pm along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, causing him to lose control of the vehicle and injure four individuals aged between 17 and 58.
The incident occurred when a 10-tonne lorry driven against the flow of traffic crashed into 11 vehicles at the Alam Budiman traffic lights. Four people were injured, one of them seriously.
In a separate court, Agilan also pleaded not guilty before Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin to self-administering methamphetamine and amphetamine at the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division office in Section 11 at about 11.30pm on the same day.
The charge, framed under Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, carries a jail term of up to two years or a fine of up to RM5,000 upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan asked for RM15,000 bail for the traffic offence and requested the court to impound the accused's driving licence. For the drug use charge, DPP Nur Amirah Zahari proposed bail of RM7,000.
Agilan's lawyer, Rohan Singh, requested minimum bail for both charges, stating that his client earns about RM1,700 a month and supports his non-working wife and an 11-year-old child.
Magistrate Ameera Mastura Khamis granted RM9,000 bail for the first charge and suspended Agilan's driving licence until the case concludes. Wan Noora Nisa set bail at RM3,900 for the second charge.
The cases have been fixed for mention on Dec 22 this year and Jan 11, 2027, respectively. — BERNAMA

Title: [UPDATED] MyEG Group companies under probe over RM230.9mil untransferred government revenue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have launched an investigation into the failure to transfer more than RM230.9 million in government revenue collections involving two companies under the MyEG Group.
Federal Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said the investigation involved MY E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Berhad following a police report lodged on Oct 7.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 409 of the Penal Code for criminal breach of trust.
"The investigation concerns the suspected failure to transfer government revenue collections amounting to RM230,913,503.55 involving the two companies," he said in a statement.
Rusdi said police had so far recorded statements from six witnesses to assist investigations.
He said several others would also be summoned to have their statements recorded as investigators worked to establish the circumstances surrounding the transactions.
"Relevant documents have been obtained and are currently being scrutinised," he said.
Section 409 of the Penal Code provides for imprisonment of between two and 20 years, whipping and a possible fine upon conviction.
It was reported that the
Road Transport Department (RTD) suspended
the services of My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd, both under the MYEG Group, as its collection agents effective Oct 5.
RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the decision was made after considering the companies' compliance with the terms and conditions of the agreement, as well as their outstanding obligations that remained unresolved.
The suspension comes after the Transport Ministry separately confirmed to business news portal The Edge that Zetrix AI owes the government more than RM200 million in unremitted collections.
The amount involves money collected from customers for vehicle road tax renewals, driving licence renewals and traffic summonses.
The Straits Times, citing official documents, reported that the
unremitted collections
dated from the start of Zetrix AI's 3-year contract with RTD in May 2023.
Zetrix AI was formerly known as MYEG Services Bhd.
The company has provided online government services, including those linked to RTD, since 2000.

Title: Experts urge 'immediate changes' to prevent rogue AI
Article:
PARIS: More than 200 artificial intelligence and cybersecurity researchers called Tuesday for immediate action to prevent further cases of AI models going rogue and posing a risk to critical infrastructure.
The letter signed by luminaries in the field including Nobel-prize winner Geoffrey Hinton and Turing Award winner Yoshua Bengio – both seen as godfathers of AI – called for models relating to cybersecurity be physically cut off from the internet during testing.
"We, the undersigned scientists, contend that both more AI safety research and more emphasis on containment technologies and procedures are needed," said the researchers in the letter.
Leading US-based AI firms have disclosed over recent months a series of incidents where models under development have escaped containment measures to access the internet and have gone on to hack websites, including gaining unauthorised access to Australian government sites.
"Without immediate changes in AI development and deployment practices, such incidents will continue to occur, and future incidents will be far more damaging to our exposed critical infrastructure," they warned.
Their letter called for organisations developing, deploying, and testing cyber-capable AI models be air-gapped – that is physically cut off from the internet – to ensure they do not escape.
It also called for the creation of an international body that standardises best practices regarding security.
The letter urged companies to be required to report containment failures to the body, which would be responsible for tracking and recording them.
"This transparency is required for both learning and accountability purposes," the letter said.
The rogue incidents amplified calls to slow AI development, but the industry and governments are divided on tapping the brakes as well as regulating the sector.
In the United States, the Trump administration opposes any binding regulation that could hinder innovation, amid fierce competition with China, and instead promoted a voluntary code of conduct.
No federal law specifically governs these models in the United States.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget debate: Bachok MP calls for fixed federal-state revenue sharing formula
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The success of the 2027 Budget depends on closer cooperation between the federal and state governments, with states given greater flexibility to determine their development priorities, said Bachok member of parliament Mohd Syahir Sulaiman.
Speaking during the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat today, he called for a fixed revenue-sharing formula that recognised states' contributions and faster implementation of federal projects, particularly in rural areas.
Citing his constituency as an example, he said a hospital project in Bachok had received four or five extensions of time (EOTs), while delays to other federal projects had driven up costs and affected the public.
He also called for greater flexibility for states to attract investment and create job opportunities for graduates and young people, reducing the need for them to migrate to cities.
"Give more flexible space to the states to attract investments to create job opportunities for graduates and youths, so they do not have to migrate to the cities," he said.
Syahir said demands concerning petroleum, taxation and development allocations should be resolved fairly, particularly those involving Sabah, Sarawak, Kelantan and Terengganu.
He also called for stronger monitoring, auditing and accountability to ensure public spending benefited the people, with economic growth translating into higher incomes, fairer wealth distribution and prudent management of public funds.
Referring to the National Pact (Wa'ad Nasional), a term introduced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during his 2027 Budget speech, Syahir said agreements between the federal and state governments must be honoured and disputes resolved through dialogue.
"As the term goes, covenants. Agreements must be obeyed, and through every difference and dispute, they should be resolved through dialogue and balanced federal-state negotiations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iskandar Puteri council nabs five strays following dog attacks
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: The Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) has caught five stray dogs following reports of dog attacks in Lima Kedai yesterday.
Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad said the operation would continue in a bid to protect residents, particularly children in residential areas.
He said MBIP personnel were called into action after Lima Kedai residents lodged reports that several of them were chased and attacked by stray dogs on the same day.
He said MBIP will conduct sustained enforcement operations and establish a special team to address the stray dog problem.
"Stray dogs pose a potential threat to residents, especially children playing in housing areas," Pandak said.
He cautioned against merely catching dogs in one area and relocating them elsewhere, saying this would not resolve the problem.
Pandak also called on dog owners not to allow their pets to roam freely. He said the local authorities must ensure that owners comply with dog licensing requirements, including measures to protect public safety.
He said any capture operation must follow established standard operating procedures, with public safety and community well-being remaining the priority.
The operation came a day after a 7-year-old boy was attacked by a pack of eight stray dogs at a
playground near a flat
in Lima Kedai, Gelang Patah. The boy sustained severe injuries to his face.
An 18-year-old youth narrowly escaped a similar attack by the same pack at the location earlier that morning.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Boy attacked by pack of stray dogs while out buying medicine
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 15-year-old boy who was fleeing a pack of strays was bitten by one of the dogs at Perumahan Rakyat Lima Kedai yesterday.
Mohammad Aliff Najmi Mohd Razi had gone out to buy fever medicine for his younger sibling when the attack occurred.
He said he heard the dogs barking but did not expect them to charge at him.
The pack, he said, immediately chased him.
He ran from Block C towards Block L to escape but fell. It was then that the dogs attacked him.
"One dog bit my leg. I screamed for help and kicked its head until it released its grip.
"I then ran upstairs to Block L. That was when my friends and several residents came to my help and chased the dogs away," he said.
Aliff said this was his first time being attacked by dogs, and said it left him traumatised.
His mother, Norazila Abdul Salam, 44, said she became concerned after Aliff didn't return after two hours.
"A friend came to tell me that my son was bitten by a dog. I was shocked when he returned with blood covering his leg, and the bleeding would not stop.
"I took him to a nearby clinic. I hope immediate action is taken to prevent this from happening again," she said.
The incident comes a day after a 7-year-old boy was attacked by a pack of eight stray dogs at a playground near a flat in Lima Kedai,
Gelang Patah
. The boy sustained severe injuries to his face.
An 18-year-old youth narrowly escaped a similar attack by the same pack at the location earlier that morning.

Title: Kelantan breaks new ground with RM35mil social sukuk, Malaysia's first by state agency
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Permodalan Kelantan Bhd has issued RM35 million in social sukuk, marking Malaysia's first such issuance by a state agency and the first in Kelantan.
The issuance was made under its RM300 million sukuk Wakalah, following its inaugural RM265 million sukuk issuance in November 2025, which was also the first sukuk in Kelantan.
Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as the sole principal adviser, lead arranger, lead manager and sustainability structuring adviser, while Maybank Islamic Bhd was the Shariah adviser and sole subscriber.
Permodalan Kelantan chairman Datuk Ahmad Yaakob said the issuance would provide an important source of financing to expand the company's Ar-Rahn Islamic pawnbroking business and widen access to Islamic financial services.
"The issuance of this social sukuk not only provides us with an important source of financing but also serves as a catalyst for the expansion of the Ar-Rahn business and enhances our capacity to provide wider access to Islamic financial services for the community," he said.
Permodalan Kelantan established its Ar-Rahn Islamic pawnbroking business on March 12, 1992, becoming Malaysia's first commercial Islamic pawnbroking institution
Ar-Rahn currently operates 35 branches across nine states, including Kelantan, Pahang, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Kedah, Perlis, Johor, Sabah and Sarawak.
The financing will strengthen Ar-Rahn's operations and financing capacity, while supporting the opening of new branches in high-potential locations.
The expansion is expected to improve Permodalan Kelantan's income-generating capacity and contribute to the overall performance of its parent company, Perbadanan Kemajuan Iktisad Negeri Kelantan (PKINK).
The expansion would also benefit micro-entrepreneurs and underserved communities by providing access to inclusive financing.
Permodalan Kelantan established a social finance framework to support the issuance, which received a "Gold" impact assessment from independent reviewer MARC Solutions Sdn Bhd.
The framework aligns with the Securities Commission Sustainable and Responsible Investment Sukuk Framework, the Asean Social Bond Standards and the International Capital Market Association's Social Bond Principles.
Maybank IB deputy chief executive officer Tengku Ariff Azhar Tengku Mohamed said the transaction demonstrated the role of capital markets in channelling funding towards social outcomes.
Maybank's involvement is also aligned with its ROAR30 targets to mobilise RM300 billion in sustainable finance by 2030, following RM176.12 billion mobilised between 2021 and 2025.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Middle East LNG industry remains hostage of Iran war
Article:
WHILE Middle Eastern oil exports have rebounded in recent weeks, Qatar's vast liquefied natural gas export facilities remain hobbled.
Until a durable resolution of the US-Israeli war with Iran is reached, Gulf shipments will be heavily curtailed, leaving the global LNG market seriously strained.
Qatar is the world's second-largest producer of LNG behind the United States. It accounts for around a fifth of global capacity at nearly 80 million metric tonnes per year.
The Iran war, now in its eighth month, has dealt a heavy blow to Qatar. The country was forced to shut down much of its main LNG complex at Ras Laffan shortly after the start of hostilities and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian missile attacks also knocked out around 17 per cent of Qatar's export capacity, costing the country tens of billions of dollars in lost annual revenue and inflicting damage that could take years to repair.
The economic blow has been among the biggest in the region. The International Monetary Fund forecasts Qatar's gross domestic product will contract by 8.6 per cent in 2026, compared with pre-war expectations for 6.1 per cen t growth.
The severe disruption to Qatar's LNG exports, alongside a drop in exports from neighbouring United Arab Emirates, has sent shockwaves through global gas markets.
The supply hit was partially cushioned by a sharp increase in US exports, which rose by around 14 per cent in 2026 from a year earlier to 123 million tonnes — but the gap in the global LNG market remained large.
The impact was felt most acutely in Asia and Europe, which rely heavily on LNG imports and have limited alternatives to replace disrupted Gulf supplies. Asian and European LNG prices hit their highest level since early 2023 in late September, nearly tripling from pre-Iran war levels.
While QatarEnergy, the country's national energy company, has indicated it will be able to restart LNG production within weeks once Hormuz reopens, LNG importers should not get too optimistic.
A deeper look at Qatar's current situation suggests its LNG industry won't be returning to pre-war norms any time soon.
The outlook for Gulf crude exports certainly has improved. Iran's grip on Hormuz appears to have weakened in recent weeks, allowing a sharp increase in oil exports from the region.
Middle East crude shipments through Hormuz rose in September to around 80 per cent of pre-war levels at 16 million barrels per day, according to data analytics firm Kpler.
Producers appear increasingly confident transiting the waterway with US Navy support, even as Iran's strikes on shipping have risen in recent weeks to the highest number since the war began.
The increase in exports has allowed Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait and Iraq to raise domestic production meaningfully.
Yet LNG traffic in the Gulf has barely recovered.
While Qatar's LNG exports rose in September to their highest level since the start of the conflict at 1.6 million tons, that was still less than a quarter of the pre-war average, according to Kpler.
Importantly, around a third of September's exports went to Kuwait, meaning they stayed inside the Gulf. The remaining volumes went to China, India and other Asian countries, with tankers typically switching off their satellite navigation systems when crossing Hormuz.
The outlook isn't improving. Qatar's October LNG exports are on track to fall sharply to just 0.6 million tons, according to Kpler, probably as a result of the rise in attacks on ships.
And last month QatarEnergy extended force majeure notices, signalling that it remains unable to deliver LNG cargoes to many customers in Asia and Europe.
The contrast between the recovery in oil exports and stagnant LNG exports reflects fundamental differences in how the two industries operate.
Oil systems are flexible. They can restart relatively quickly and benefit from extensive storage and shipping logistics. LNG supply chains, on the other hand, are highly integrated, capital intensive and far less tolerant of disruption.
Qatar's LNG facilities consist of 14 production units — known as trains — supplied by gas from the offshore North Field, the world's largest gas reservoir, which the country shares with Iran.
North Field production has been running at minimal rates since the start of the war, just enough to meet Qatar's domestic needs and maintain limited exports.
Restarting the system is not simply a matter of reopening a terminal or dispatching a few tankers.
To increase LNG exports, Qatar would first need to raise gas production. And that is where the logistical challenges become quite complex.
The raw gas extracted from the North Field contains large volumes of very light oil known as condensate, which must be separated and exported.
If condensate cannot be shipped out reliably, Qatar risks quickly running out of storage. It could then be forced to curb gas production regardless of LNG demand.
Similarly, Qatar has limited capacity to store LNG itself in onshore tanks or aboard vessels at sea, leaving little room for operational delays if exports are interrupted.
Finally, the global LNG tanker fleet is far smaller than the oil tanker fleet. Freight rates are therefore much higher, while shippers are far less willing to send expensive LNG carriers through Hormuz if there is any risk they could become trapped inside the Gulf for weeks or, worse, get hit by an Iranian strike.
Qatar therefore needs more than occasional safe passage through Hormuz. It needs assurance that all ships will be able to transit the waterway safely.
The timing is particularly unfortunate because Qatar is in the middle of a massive expansion programme that will see it raise LNG capacity to 142 million tons per year by 2030.
That would give it roughly a quarter of the global market. But new capacity is of little value if the export route remains uncertain.
Until the strait's security is governed by a credible and durable agreement involving Iran, the United States and regional powers, the world's largest LNG expansion project may remain stranded.
In the meantime, the global LNG market has little hope of a speedy recovery.biggest news in markets and finance seven days a week.
