Title: Cross-border haze to ease in two weeks as monsoon transition begins, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The cross-border haze that has affected Malaysia’s air quality since August 8 is expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks as wind patterns change, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said.
He said Malaysia had entered the monsoon transition phase on October 9, with the northeast monsoon expected to begin towards the end of this month.
“However, I want to emphasise that changes in weather conditions alone are not a long-term solution to the haze issue. It could happen again.
“Fire prevention efforts must therefore address the problem at its source. Domestic enforcement must be strengthened, while regional cooperation must be enhanced to reduce the risk of similar incidents recurring,” he said during the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Syed Ibrahim was responding to concerns raised by Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who described the haze as a national crisis affecting public health, safety, the economy and public well-being.
The issue was also raised by Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching) and Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong).
Yii said the haze was no longer merely a seasonal nuisance but an annual emergency requiring stronger action, including the proposed introduction of a Cross-Border Haze Pollution Act and greater transparency in sharing hotspot data and information on plantation concessions.
Young Syefura, meanwhile, sought clarification on the government’s diplomatic engagements with Indonesia, including the responses received and the effectiveness of the measures taken.
She also called for stronger domestic enforcement and better protection for vulnerable groups.
In his response, Syed Ibrahim said the latest haze episode was caused by an increase in forest and land fires in several parts of Indonesia, including Kalimantan and Sumatra, which had affected air quality in Malaysia, particularly in Sarawak.
He said the Department of Environment (DOE) received 2,104 complaints concerning open burning and carried out 3,039 enforcement actions between August 3 and October 9.
These comprised 2,104 monitoring actions, 168 field orders, 32 notices, 13 compounds and two court actions.
As part of the mitigation efforts, the government also conducted 11 cloud seeding operations between August 30 and October 15 in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department, the National Disaster Management Agency and the Malaysian Army.
“The main challenge in enforcing laws with cross-border elements is obtaining sufficient evidence to establish the source of pollution and identify the parties responsible,” he said.
Syed Ibrahim added that the ministry had yet to receive any official information from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities regarding the alleged involvement of Malaysian companies in open-burning incidents in Indonesia. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Kedah schools to operate as usual tomorrow as API readings remain moderate
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 13 — All schools in Kedah will operate as usual tomorrow, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings across the state remaining below 100 as of 2pm today.
In a statement, the Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said any decisions on school closures or reopening due to the haze would be subject to the Education Ministry’s directives, based on JPN’s monitoring of daily API readings and local developments.
“Kedah JPN will continue to monitor the situation and coordinate with the District Education Offices and schools to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Home Ministry to seek details on five Malaysians held in Japan drug bust, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 13 — The Home Ministry will contact Japanese authorities to obtain accurate information on the arrest of Malaysians suspected of involvement in a drug case in Japan.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he had instructed Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan to act immediately to establish the facts.
“Complete information on the incident will be conveyed to the media as soon as it is received,” he told reporters after the Madani Townhall session between Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Kedah students and the Home Minister here today.
He was commenting on the arrest of five Malaysians, including a woman, at Haneda Airport in Tokyo last Saturday on suspicion of attempting to smuggle about five kilogrammes (kg) of cocaine worth ¥120 million (RM3.1 million).
According to Fuji News Network (FNN), the operation was uncovered after customs officers became suspicious of a suspect wearing shoes with unusually thick soles.
FNN reported that the suspects were believed to have concealed the drugs beneath their shoe insoles when boarding a flight from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), before customs inspections upon arrival in Japan exposed the alleged smuggling attempt.
Saifuddin Nasution said the Home Ministry’s move was also in line with the approach taken in the case involving the arrest of a Malaysian co-pilot in Jakarta several months ago, as well as the seizure of 521 kg of drugs from a private jet in Laos, which was initially alleged to have originated from Malaysia.
Meanwhile, he said the implementation of 17 recommendations or initiatives undertaken through a joint committee comprising the Home Ministry and the Transport Ministry (MOT) to strengthen security at KLIA and the country’s entry points would continue as planned.
He said the initiatives would be implemented in three phases, with the first focusing on destinations identified as high-risk areas or hotspots.
“For destinations listed as hotspots, comprehensive screening of passengers, including body and baggage checks, will be carried out on 100 per cent of passengers,” he said.
However, he said destinations in Japan, including Tokyo, were not included in the original list of hotspots. — Bernama

Title: Businessman sentenced to six months’ jail, ordered to pay RM5,000 for assaulting ex-girlfriend
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 13 — A businessman was sentenced to six months’ jail by the Magistrate’s Court here today for assaulting his former girlfriend, causing injuries to her eyes and body, two years ago.
Magistrate Amira Sariaty Zainal imposed the sentence on Hoh Peng Onn, 47, after the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt at the end of the defence case.
“The court orders that the prison sentence take effect from the date of conviction today. The accused must also pay RM5,000 in compensation to the victim, taking into account the trauma, injuries and emotional distress she suffered,” Amira Sariaty said.
The court also ordered that Hoh serve an additional two months in jail if he failed to pay the compensation today.
However, the court allowed an application by defence counsel Cheow Wee to stay the prison sentence pending an appeal to the High Court, but ordered that the compensation be paid today.
Hoh was charged with intentionally causing hurt to Liaw Ju Shuang, 28, at a residence in Putra Permai Town Centre, Seri Kembangan, at 12.30am on October 5, 2024.
The charge was brought under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
In her judgment, Amira Sariaty said that although the neighbour, the third prosecution witness, did not witness the assault, the witness saw the victim with a bleeding head and bruises around her eyes and other parts of her body when she sought help.
“The witness also contacted the police, who took the victim to hospital for treatment. There was no reason for the victim to fabricate a story to frame the accused.
“In view of this, the court finds that the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt against the prosecution’s case, and was merely a denial unsupported by strong evidence and testimony,” Amira Sariaty said.
During mitigation, the defence sought a fine, citing the accused’s eyesight problems, which it said would make imprisonment difficult for him.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Syed Ahmed Khabir Abdul Rahman sought a jail term and a fine, arguing that the public interest outweighed that of the accused, given the extent of the victim’s injuries, and requested that compensation be awarded to her. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Malaysia’s 3.3pc fiscal deficit target achievable, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia is capable of achieving its fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) under Budget 2027, provided the assumptions underpinning the budget hold amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, said Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
The Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman, who is also a senior political advisor to the Prime Minister and a former Finance Minister, noted that the country’s fiscal position had improved over the past three years.
“When we look at the fiscal discipline that we have demonstrated over the last three years, with the fiscal deficit at around 5.5 per cent in 2022, we are moving in the right direction.
“If we look at government revenue and the country’s GDP growth, we should be able to achieve the 3.3 per cent target, provided the global geopolitical situation, the various challenges facing the world, oil prices and the other assumptions underpinning the budget remain as expected,” Tengku Zafrul said to Bernama.
He described Budget 2027 as a responsible budget that balances investment incentives with efforts to ensure that economic growth benefits a wider segment of Malaysians and businesses.
He noted that the budget took into account the interests of different stakeholders, while seeking to strengthen economic growth and ensure that its benefits reached both lower-income groups and businesses.
“If you look at it objectively, it is a well-thought-out and balanced budget that takes into account the interests of all stakeholders while ensuring that both the lower- and higher-income groups are supported,” he said.
On investment prospects, Tengku Zafrul said planned capital expenditure by government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) could generate positive spillover effects for the broader economy.
He said investments by Khazanah Nasional Bhd, the Employees Provident Fund and other institutions, as well as capital expenditure by Petronas sent positive signals to potential investors, as domestic investment commitments could help strengthen foreign investors’ confidence in Malaysia.
“I believe that these are good for investors to take note of, because when they come to invest in a country, they also want to see confidence, and if our own companies or institutions are investing, then they will also be more comfortable or more confident in doing so,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Senior govt agency official, company director remanded seven days in bribery probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — A senior official of a government agency and a company director have been remanded for seven days for allegedly soliciting and receiving bribes totalling about RM15,000.
The bribes were believed to be an inducement to secure supply work at the government agency.
Magistrate Aliaa Anwar issued the remand order against both men, effective from today until Oct 19, following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court this morning.
It is understood that both suspects, in their 50s and 60s, were detained at 2pm yesterday when they went to give their statements at the Kuala Lumpur MACC office.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects allegedly colluded in the act between 2021 and 2023.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohammad Zakkuan Talib, when contacted, confirmed the remand.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: STAM and MUET examinations in Pahang to continue as planned despite haze
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 13 — The Sijil Tinggi Agama Malaysia (STAM) and Malaysian University English Test (MUET) examinations in Pahang will proceed as scheduled despite the haze.
In a statement, the Pahang State Education Department (JPN) said the examinations would be conducted in accordance with the standard operating procedures (SOP) and safety measures in force.
“Students attending school, including those sitting for ongoing examinations, are encouraged to wear face masks to protect their health,” it said.
Candidates and examination personnel were advised to refer to their schools, examination centres and the department’s official channels for further notifications and instructions.
Meanwhile, all educational institutions under Pahang JPN in Rompin, Pekan and Kuantan will be closed tomorrow due to the haze affecting the districts.
The department said any changes to the operational status of educational institutions and their reopening would be announced through its official channels and the respective District Education Offices, based on prevailing conditions and safety considerations.
Pahang JPN will continue to monitor the situation in coordination with the three district education offices and relevant agencies to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of students and education personnel. — Bernama

Title: Teachers union: RM69b education allocation must bring real improvements to Malaysian schools
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Better school facilities, improved safety and a more conducive learning environment are among the key improvements the school community hopes to see from the increased allocation for education in Budget 2027.
West Malaysia Malay Teachers Union (KGMMB) president Dr Mohd Sobri Yusuf said the RM69 billion allocation, up from RM66.2 billion this year, should translate into meaningful improvements in schools, with its success measured by the actual benefits delivered to teachers and students.
“Regardless of how much is allocated, the desired outcomes will not be achieved unless the funding brings about positive and tangible changes,” he said on Bernama TV’s Apa Khabar Malaysia talk show today.
Mohd Sobri said the higher school maintenance allocation, which has doubled to RM2 billion, could deliver direct benefits to school communities, particularly in ensuring that learning facilities were safe and comfortable.
“Safety must come first, and maintenance funds should go to schools that need them most, especially for repairs such as leaking roofs and faulty wiring, so that students and teachers can learn and work in a safe and comfortable environment,” he said.
Mohd Sobri said the recruitment of 200 teaching assistants for primary schools with large numbers of pupils could help reduce teachers’ workload, allowing them to focus more on teaching and students’ learning needs.
On the Supplementary Food Programme (RMT), he said its implementation must be closely monitored to ensure students received meals that met the required quality standards and complied with the prescribed menu and portion sizes.
Meanwhile, Federation of Peninsular Malay Students (GPMS) president Muhd Fazreen Ismadi Fauzi said increasing the Early Schooling Assistance (BAP) to RM200 would help parents, particularly those from the B40 group, meet the cost of preparing their children for school.
However, he stressed that the increase in aid should be accompanied by measures to keep school supplies affordable and provide lasting relief to families.
On the RM2,500 allowance for Form Six students, Muhd Fazreen suggested that the aid be disbursed monthly rather than in a lump sum, allowing students to manage their educational expenses more effectively throughout the year.
“For GPMS, it would be better to pay the allowance monthly rather than in one lump sum. If students receive the full amount at once, they might spend it in a day on things like mobile phones, and the money may not last them through the year,” he said.
He added that aid distribution must be closely monitored to ensure the funds reach the intended recipients without any leakage.
Muhd Fazreen also stressed the need to ensure school facilities cater to students with disabilities, particularly with the planned enrolment of six-year-olds in Year One from 2027.
He said schools must be equipped with suitable facilities and support services to meet the needs of all students. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi proposes initiative to preserve speeches, writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today has proposed a national initiative to preserve and revive historical speeches and writings of Malaysia’s founding leaders for future generations.
He said the initiative, inspired by the reprint of pioneering journalist J. Victor Morais’ Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians, could involve retrieving rare speeches, writings and historical accounts from archives.
“I will discuss with National Unity Minister (Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang) to identify the most appropriate steps. If possible, we will work towards organising something in conjunction with National Month celebrations next year.”
Fahmi said this at the launch of Great Wisdom of the First Malaysians – A Reprint of Selected Speeches by Pioneering Journalist J. Victor Morais here today.
Also present were Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) editor-in-chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj, Daily Express chief editor Datuk Sardahthisa James and Victor’s son Benedict Morais.
Fahmi said the collection highlighted the importance of preserving the intellectual contributions and perspectives of the country’s founding figures, particularly at a time when rapid development and the pursuit of future progress could overshadow an understanding of the nation’s past.
The communications minister said the book deserved wider circulation beyond its initial print run of 2,000 copies to ensure its valuable historical content reached a broader audience.
In this regard, Fahmi offered to help raise funds to print an additional 2,000 copies, subject to the agreement of those involved in the publication, and proposed organising a related programme at Parliament next year.
He said he would distribute copies to all Cabinet ministers at Friday’s meeting to highlight the importance of understanding Malaysia’s nation-building history.
Meanwhile, Sardahthisa, also known as James Sarda, said the book provided valuable insights into the aspirations of Malaysia’s founding leaders and the challenges they faced during the country’s formation, making it an important resource for researchers, policymakers and younger generations.
He collaborated with Benedict to republish the collection, originally released in 1967 under the title Selected Speeches.
“For journalists like me, finding speeches delivered by Tunku Abdul Rahman and Tun Abdul Razak in Parliament is not easy, as record-keeping was different in those days and access to parliamentary records involved various protocols.
“This book is a gold mine for research. It is a one-stop centre containing the speeches of leaders from various backgrounds and their hopes for Malaysia,” he told reporters after the event.
Meanwhile, Benedict recalled that his father was a self-taught journalist who honed his skills through a correspondence course at Rapid Results College (RRC) in London at a time when formal journalism training was not widely available.
The 80-year-old said his father later gained practical experience through on-the-job training, reflecting the determination and initiative that shaped his career in journalism.
Recalling the declaration of independence on Aug 31, 1957, Benedict said he was a 12-year-old student among the 25,000 people who witnessed the historic occasion at Merdeka Stadium, including Tunku Abdul Rahman’s seven resounding cries of “Merdeka”.
He also recalled the strong sense of unity among the people during that period, when they simply identified themselves as Malayans regardless of race.
“We saw ourselves as Malayans…neighbours kept their homes open, shared food and visited one another freely. It was a spirit of unity that came naturally rather than being imposed,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Orang Asli children should not be denied documentation over parents’ marriage records, says National Registration Dept
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 13 — Orang Asli children should not be left without documentation because of issues involving their parents’ marriage records, said National Registration Department (JPN) director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias.
He said JPN would assess each case based on the facts, supporting documents and individual circumstances to determine the appropriate action, particularly for birth registration.
He said the department respected the customs and culture of the Orang Asli community, but customary marriages and the legal requirements for marriage registration had to be assessed in accordance with the applicable laws.
“Children should not be left without documentation assistance just because their parents face marriage record issues. We respect customs, obey the law and help find solutions,” he told reporters after attending the Registration Literacy Programme held in conjunction with the 78th state-level National Registration Day celebration at Pos Balar here.
Badrul Hisham said each case had to be assessed individually, with no automatic conclusions drawn about the recognition of customary marriages without considering the specific facts and circumstances.
He said 143 New Generation MyKads had been issued to the Orang Asli community in Kelantan through the MEKAR Programme, which brings registration services closer to the community.
He clarified that the figure referred only to MyKads issued through the programme and did not represent the total number of new MyKads issued to the Orang Asli community in the state.
JPN was also obtaining identification data from the Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) to determine how many Orang Asli in Kelantan did not have a MyKad or birth certificate as of 2026.
“The data will be used to help JPN review records and mobilise the MEKAR Programme, thereby ensuring that identified cases receive follow-up action and appropriate documentation assistance,” he said.
He said the total number of Orang Asli without the documents could not yet be confirmed as JPN had not received the data from JAKOA.
On another matter, Badrul Hisham said JPN had also identified issues involving permanent resident card (MyPR) or red MyKad holders, but the latest total was still being verified before it could be announced.
JPN stressed that each case had to be assessed based on the individual’s status and documentation to ensure the appropriate action was taken. — Bernama

Title: Body wrapped in cloth found in drain at Sama Gagah market in Penang
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Oct 13 — A man’s body wrapped in cloth was found in a drain at Sama Gagah Public Market here at about 7am today.
Penang Police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng, when contacted by Bernama, confirmed the discovery and said investigations were underway to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and the cause of death.
“The body has been sent to Seberang Jaya Hospital for a post-mortem,” he said.
Several photographs showing the body had earlier gone viral on social media. — Bernama

Title: MACC records RM1.27b in asset freezes from 2022 to September, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) recorded asset freezes worth RM1.27 billion from 2022 to September this year, involving bank accounts, jewellery, immovable property and other valuables.
Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said the asset freezes were carried out under Section 44 of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613).
He said 1,336 asset-freezing orders were issued under the Act in 2025, while another 1,006 were issued from Jan 1 to Sept 30 this year.
A total of 481 freezing orders were revoked without charges in 2025, while another 781 were revoked in the first nine months of this year, he added.
“The withdrawal, cancellation or variation of an asset-freezing order does not necessarily mean that no offence has occurred or that the investigation has no basis.
“This is because freezing assets is part of the investigative process and an enforcement measure to prevent assets suspected of being linked to an offence from being transferred, disposed of or traded,” he said.
He was answering a question from Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong on the power to freeze assets under Section 44 of Act 613, as well as regulatory and investigative issues involving the MACC, during the Special Chamber sitting in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Kulasegaran said investigations conducted by the MACC and other enforcement agencies were not carried out arbitrarily, but in accordance with established criteria.
He said preliminary action was taken based on reports, prima facie investigations and the presence of suspicious transactions, such as unusually large sums of money moving in and out of accounts.
The 90-day period provided under Section 44 of Act 613 allows a freezing order to be revoked as soon as possible once an investigation has been completed, he added.
“I agree with the Honourable Member that having a law such as the one in Singapore, which is more independent and impartial ... would be better if it were left to the courts.
“This is something I have read about and examined, and I have told the agency concerned to look into it because it would be a win-win position, and the MACC’s good name would be respected,” he said.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Wee on the need to tighten governance, including requiring court approval before freezing accounts or seizing assets belonging to listed companies, to protect the interests of minority shareholders. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 should accelerate transition from R&D to Malaysian technology, says Mimos
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The government’s continued focus on strengthening the technology and innovation ecosystem through Budget 2027 provides an opportunity to accelerate the transition from research and development (R&D) to commercialisation, industry adoption and tangible economic value, said Mimos Bhd (Mimos).
It said the government’s commitment to advancing Malaysia’s technology and innovation agenda, particularly through the Finance Ministry (MOF) and Science, Technology and Innovation Ministry (Mosti), would help strengthen the country’s R&D capabilities, develop home-grown technologies and translate innovation into economic and social benefits.
The Budget allocated RM6 billion for R&D and commercialisation activities across ministries, while Khazanah Nasional Bhd (Khazanah) and Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (KWAP) separately will invest RM1.2 billion to help local semiconductor companies move into higher-value segments.
“These measures present an opportunity to connect research capabilities more directly with national industrial priorities and market demand, including the development of higher-value technology capabilities and stronger local companies,” Mimos said in a statement today.
It said the budget also allocated RM30 million through the Malaysian Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) to help 4,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) adopt artificial intelligence (AI) and automate their operations.
It said the measures, together with initiatives to support technology startups, underscored the importance of translating local R&D into practical, industry-ready solutions that could be adopted by businesses and contribute to economic growth.
Mimos President and Group Chief Executive Officer Dr Saat Shukri Embong said the next step for Malaysia is to ensure that these capabilities translate into commercial outcomes, stronger Malaysian intellectual property (IP), industry adoption and economic value.
“The RM6 billion commitment to R&D and commercialisation is an important step in strengthening Malaysia’s technological sovereignty by building our own capabilities, developing home-grown technologies and creating greater value from Malaysian innovation,” he said.
Saat Shukri added that it is crucial for Malaysia to not simply develop more technologies, but instead focus on developing technologies that can be adopted, scaled and used by the industry.
From an operational and industry adoption perspective, Mimos’s Deputy Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Chief Operating Officer, Abdul Rashdee Abdul Kadir, said technology adoption should be able to solve real business and industry challenges, so that it can help businesses increase their productivity gains.
“Whether through AI, automation, smart manufacturing or other advanced technologies, the focus should be on enabling companies, particularly businesses that are ready to scale, improve productivity, efficiency and competitiveness,” he said.
On the other hand, Mimos’s Deputy Group Chief Executive Officer and Group Chief of Staff, Nurezmy A. Majid said sustained technology development requires a coordinated ecosystem between the government, industry, academia and R&D institutions, as it cannot happen in isolation.
“Malaysia needs a strong, connected ecosystem where policy, R&D, industry demand, talent development, and commercialisation work together. Budget 2027 is an opportunity to strengthen these linkages and ensure that national investments in technology capabilities are aligned with Malaysia’s broader economic priorities,” she said.
From a technology perspective, Mimos Group Chief Technology Officer Dr Zulaikha Kadim said the government’s effort to put quantum technology as a future skills area in the Budget reinforced the need to build expertise across strategic technologies such as AI and semiconductors that are increasingly central to economic competitiveness.
“The opportunity is not simply to adopt technologies developed elsewhere, but we should also strengthen our ability to develop, validate and commercialise technologies that carry Malaysian IP and can compete regionally and globally,” said Zulaikha.
Meanwhile, Mimos Group Chief of Corporate Planning and Strategy Dr Hazian Mamat said the Budget 2027 outcomes should be tracked through clear indicators such as industry adoption, technology readiness, Malaysian IP development, private-sector participation and commercial returns.
“We need to look beyond individual projects and consider how today’s investments build tomorrow’s capabilities. This means strengthening the pipeline from R&D to commercialisation, supporting technology adoption and developing the talent required to sustain Malaysia’s competitiveness in strategic technology sectors,” he said.
According to Hazian, this outcome-based approach would be important in ensuring that every investment in innovation contributes meaningfully to Malaysia’s long-term competitiveness. — Bernama

Title: Ministry to ensure Budget 2027 funds benefit women, children, OKU and elderly, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development’s (KPWKM) increased allocation under Budget 2027 will strengthen social protection and the well-being of target groups, including women, children, persons with disabilities (OKU) and the elderly.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, said the funding, which rose four per cent to RM4.355 billion, would support various aid initiatives, the development of a care ecosystem and economic empowerment to help target groups realise their potential and become self-reliant.
She said the key initiatives include an increase in Elderly Assistance to RM1.3 billion for nearly 200,000 recipients, and assistance for persons with disabilities to RM1.5 billion for more than 300,000 recipients.
“KPWKM’s priority is to ensure the allocation is translated into services and benefits that are truly felt by the people,” she said at a press conference at Parliament today.
Nancy said the ministry is also focusing on women’s economic empowerment through an approach that combines skills, capital or equipment assistance, support networks and market opportunities to help them generate income.
Among the initiatives are the Madani Well-Being Grant, KIRANA Programme, which provides training, equipment grants and digital marketing guidance, and KASIHNITA, which focuses on personal development and financial management for women, particularly single mothers.
On family well-being, Nancy said the government is continuing the LPPKN BuAi Programme, which offers fertility treatment subsidies of up to RM2,000 per cycle to 2,000 eligible couples, as well as fertility advocacy efforts and men’s wellness services targeting 42,000 individuals.
Meanwhile, Nancy said KPWKM plans to conduct a study to identify the factors behind the rise in stabbing cases in schools and institutions of higher learning.
She said the study is still in the planning stage and requires cooperation from other ministries, while agencies under KPWKM provide counselling services and support to victims, families and individuals who commit such acts.
Among the agencies involved are the Malaysian Board of Counsellors, the Social Welfare Department (JKM), LPPKN and the National Welfare Foundation (YKN).
On efforts to strengthen women’s safety and address femicide, Nancy said KPWKM, through JKM, the Women’s Development Department and YKN, is also working with non-governmental organisations to assist women, including shelter for those unable to return home. — Bernama

Title: Johor records nearly 10,000 commercial crime cases with RM212.64m in losses, says state top cop
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Johor police opened 9,897 investigation papers involving commercial crimes in the first nine months of this year, with losses totalling RM212.64 million.
Its chief, Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad, said the figure represented an increase of 3,036 cases from the 6,861 recorded during the same period last year, although financial losses declined from RM252.57 million.
He said more than 90 per cent of the cases reported between Jan 1 and Sept 30 involved online scams.
“The increase in reported cases calls for more proactive measures. Fraud and scams continue to evolve alongside technological advances and an increasingly sophisticated digital landscape,” he said at the Johor Police contingent’s monthly assembly here today.
Ab Rahaman said the state’s crime index also rose to 4,343 cases during the same period, compared with 4,152 last year.
Violent crimes increased to 1,123 cases from 981, while property crimes rose to 3,220 from 3,171, he added.
Separately, Ab Rahaman said police were awaiting instructions and a formal decision from the Johor State Prosecutor’s Office on whether to charge the suspect in the murder of Form Four student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal.
He said the investigation papers on the case were referred to the office on October 9.
“The suspect is a juvenile, and this requires more careful consideration by the Johor State Prosecution Director,” he said.
Irene Sofiya was found unconscious and covered in blood at a school hall in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, at about 5pm on October 3. She was later pronounced dead.
A 16-year-old boy was remanded for six days from October 4 to assist investigations, with the remand subsequently extended for another six days until Friday. — Bernama

Title: King attends pre-council meeting of Conference of Rulers at Istana Negara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today attended the pre-council meeting of the 273rd Conference of Rulers at Istana Negara.
According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page, the pre-council meeting was also attended by Tunku Temenggong Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj as the official representative of Johor Regent Tunku Mahkota Ismail.
The 273rd Meeting of the Conference of Rulers will run for two days starting tomorrow and will be presided over by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia warns of severe storms across peninsula and East Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across several states in Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah, forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 6pm today.
In an advisory released at 3.45pm, the department cautioned that adverse weather will affect commuters heading into the evening rush hour across northern, southern, and eastern corridors.
In the northern peninsula, the alert covers the entirety of Perlis and Penang.
In Kedah, stormy conditions are expected across eight districts: Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, Baling, Kuala Muda, Kulim, and Bandar Baharu.
In Perak, the warning covers Kerian, Larut, Matang dan Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, and Perak Tengah.
On the east of the peninsula, the advisory encompasses Kuala Krai, Machang, and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan, alongside Besut, Setiu, Hulu Terengganu, and Dungun in Terengganu. In Pahang, affected areas include Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Jerantut, and Kuantan.
Further south, stormy weather is forecast across Johor, covering Tangkak, Segamat, Muar, Batu Pahat, Kluang, and Kulai.
In East Malaysia, the warning spans extensive divisions across Sarawak: Betong, Sarikei, Mukah, Sibu, Bintulu, Limbang, Song in Kapit, as well as Subis and Marudi in Miri.
In Sabah, the alert covers Kudat, the West Coast division, and the Interior division (specifically Beaufort, Sipitang, and Tambunan). It also extends to Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Sandakan) and the Tawau division (Tawau, Kalabakan, and Semporna).
MetMalaysia explained that a thunderstorm warning is triggered when cloud formations indicate imminent heavy rainfall with an intensity exceeding 20 millimetres per hour, or when precipitation is expected to persist for more than an hour.
The department emphasized that these alerts serve as short-term advisories and remain valid for a maximum duration of six hours from the time of issuance.

Title: Molotov cocktail attack on Kulai Rohingya settlement linked to provocative viral clip, police say
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Police believe an early morning arson attack targeting several homes at an ethnic Rohingya settlement in Kulai Besar was triggered by racially provocative videos circulating on social media.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad confirmed that Molotov cocktails were hurled at the settlement, likely sparking localised fires along the perimeter fences of several residences.
“However, the fire was successfully extinguished and there were no injuries or other damage reported.
“Police have also received a report on the incident at 1.30am,” he said in a statement today.
Initial investigations indicate the attack could have been retaliation by individuals angered by two viral video clips circulating online.
Ab Rahaman said the footage showed a group of ethnic Rohingya youths issuing challenges for a street confrontation in the Kulai area.
“The individuals in the video also claimed that the Malay community lacked the courage to enter the area,” he said, adding that police also received a report on the videos.
In a related development, a Rohingya man in his 30s lodged a separate police report denying any involvement in the viral content, claiming that unidentified individuals had appropriated his photograph without consent to manufacture the provocative videos.
Ab Rahaman said police have launched investigations under both anti-arson statutes and cyber-crime laws.
“Police have opened two investigation papers regarding this incident. Investigators are probing the case under Section 436 of the Penal Code for mischief by fire or explosive substances.
“Police are also investigating the case under Sections 505(b) and 505(c) of the Penal Code that deal with statements, rumors, or reports that cause public mischief, fear, or communal incitement.
“The case is also being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 regarding the improper use of network facilities,” he said.
The incident highlights escalating communal friction in Malaysia, where public and political attitudes toward the displaced Rohingya community have increasingly hardened from initial humanitarian sympathy to visible resentment.
Such hostility is frequently fuelled by online misinformation, unverified social media narratives, and localised discontent with suburban migrant enclaves.
Malaysia is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention, but currently hosts more than 126,000 registered Rohingya refugees through the UNHCR.

Title: Miri-Subang flights to begin Dec 1, offering new link to Klang Valley
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Miri residents will have another air travel option when a new flight service to Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport (LTSAAS) in Subang begins operations on December 1, 2026.
Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said the new route would benefit residents who frequently travel for work, business, education, medical treatment and family commitments.
He said Subang Airport’s proximity to central Kuala Lumpur and surrounding areas would offer greater convenience to travellers, particularly in terms of accessibility and onward land transportation.
“I welcome this announcement because the addition of this route is not just about providing more flight options, but also about enhancing Miri’s connectivity with the country’s main economic centres,” he said in a statement today.
Chiew, who is also the Miri Member of Parliament, said he had previously met with Batik Air to discuss the possibility of introducing the route and welcomed the positive developments leading towards its implementation.
He said improved air connectivity could benefit the business and tourism sectors while making travel between Miri and the Klang Valley more convenient.
“I believe better air transport links are important for a city like Miri, which has tremendous potential for further growth. More flight options mean greater convenience for residents and more opportunities to stimulate local economic activity,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Deputy minister: Anti-scalping provisions to be added to Price Control Act
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living is “actively” working on a dedicated legal framework to combat ticket scalping, with new regulations expected to take effect as early as next year, Parliament was told this morning.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Deputy Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh said anti-scalping provisions could be inserted under Section 15(1) of the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act, which grants authority to introduce measures curbing unfair pricing and resale practices.
“The ministry is currently engaging in engagement sessions with event organisers and conducting benchmarking studies with the objective and intention of establishing a legal framework,” she said during Question Time.
“Under Act 723, or the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act, Section 15(1) provides the minister and the Ministry the power to establish a mechanism in the form of regulations that we can use to curb these scalping activities,” she added.
Scalping is a term used to describe the practice of buying something highly sought after like concert tickets, shoes, or clothing and then reselling it at a much higher price, leveraging scarcity and demand.
While scalping in Malaysia has been around for some time, backlash against the practice blew up when British rock giants Coldplay came to perform in Kuala Lumpur in 2023, when scalpers bought tickets in big numbers and then resell them at exorbitant rates.
For example, the standard CAT 1 tickets that were originally priced at RM1,288 were re-listed for reportedly up to RM43,000, sparking outrage.
Investigative reports suggest scalping in Malaysia has evolved from individuals reselling a few extra tickets into an organised, tech-driven operation affecting multiple sectors as scalpers began utilising internet bots to make bulk purchases.
Bots help resellers bypass virtual waiting rooms to buy bulk batches of tickets within seconds before human buyers even load the payment page.
Fuziah said the anti-scalping provisions would include the definition of scalping itself, how to control bulk ticket purchasing activities and enforcing the use identification or names on ticket purchases.
“Because when bulk ticket purchases happen — whether through bots or by individuals — this is where secondary sales or a secondary layer of sales occur,” she said.
“So that is where the situation of scalping may arise. This is what we are studying.”

Title: Penang’s Jalan Magazine slip road to face periodic closures from Oct 14 until Feb 21 next year for Mutiara Line LRT works
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 13 — Part of the route along Jalan Magazine here will be closed periodically for 131 days starting tomorrow to make way for construction work on the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) Project.
In a statement today, Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) said the long-term closure will start from 10am tomorrow and continue until 5am on February 21, 2027.
“The closure involves the slip road from Lebuh McNair near 1st Avenue Mall towards Jalan Magazine up to the front of Hotel Jen heading towards Komtar.
“However, other routes will remain open for traffic use,” the statement read.
MRT Corp said the closure will facilitate construction work on the Mutiara Line LRT Project under Package CMC1, including road widening and utility relocation works.
Motorists are therefore advised to exercise caution when passing through the area. Signboards, traffic cones and flagmen will be stationed at the location to manage traffic and ensure safety. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s semiconductor exports remain exempt from US tariffs, says Johari Ghani
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia continues to enjoy tariff exemptions for its semiconductor exports to the United States, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister (Miti) Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He emphasised that Malaysia has yet to receive any indication that Washington will impose tariffs on the sector’s exports.
“We have not received any indication that the US will impose tariffs on Malaysian semiconductors at this time,” said Johari in a press conference at the European Union-Malaysia Business Day 2026: Selangor in Focus here today.
He said negotiations with the US under Section 301 covered four issues, namely forced labour, excess production capacity, the environmental standards and government subsidies.
“Environment and state subsidies, we are fine. We are not subject to anything because we are clear.
“The forced labour issue has been finalised, with Malaysia subject to a 10 per cent rate, compared with 12.5 per cent for other countries. Only 17 economies have been charged 10 per cent.
“The only thing that is not finalised is excess capacity. We do not have excess capacity,” said Johari.
He said that any excess capacity associated with goods exported from Malaysia could be from third countries, adding that Malaysia would seek clarification from the US on the countries identified as contributing to the issue.
“That (excess capacity) is from a third country. We will commit (but) they must give us a list that they assume is a country that is subject to excess capacity. Then we will take them out from our list,” said Johari.
He said access to overseas markets depended on meeting the respective countries’ requirements and regulations.
“At the end of the day, any market that you want to go to is up to them. What are their criteria? What is the law that we need to comply with? Then we need to comply; otherwise you cannot go,” he said.
Johari said the EU imposed strict environmental requirements on its trading partners.
“As long as you can comply, then that is it. Likewise, I think any other country does not matter. Everyone has a unique requirement,” he said.
The EU-Malaysia Business Day 2026: Selangor in Focus was held in conjunction with the Selangor International Business Summit (SIBS), scheduled from October 14 to 17, 2026.
Hosted by the Delegation of the European Union to Malaysia, the third edition of the annual flagship event was organised in collaboration with the Selangor state government, Invest Selangor and Eurocham Malaysia.
Held under the theme “Bridging Innovation-Powering Progress”, the event aimed to advance business ties and further unlock investment opportunities involving the substantial EU business presence in Malaysia.
With over 550 EU companies operating in Selangor, generating a total annual revenue of over RM51 billion, the event highlights high-growth and high-value sectors such as advanced manufacturing, green transition, digitalisation and logistics.
Also present were EU Commissioner for International Partnerships, Jozef Sikela, and Ambassador of the EU to Malaysia, Rafael Daerr.
Sikela said that investing alongside Malaysia would strengthen and diversify the semiconductor ecosystem on which both economies increasingly depend.
“We live in a world of geopolitical tensions, economic disruptions and growing competition over critical technologies in the world, which is becoming more and more like a world where controversial and resilient supply chains and trusted, mutually beneficial partnerships matter more than ever,” he said.
Sikela said the resumption of negotiations on the Malaysia-EU Free Trade Agreement (MEUFTA) would further deepen economic ties, citing Lumut Maritime Industrial City as another potential area for collaboration.
“The Lumut Maritime Industrial City is another good example of opportunities ahead, bringing together infrastructure, industry, logistics and potential for greener maritime activities,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina: Schools in Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and nine districts to close tomorrow as haze lingers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Schools in Johor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan will stay closed tomorrow, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek announced today, as haze continues to affect parts of the country.
Schools under nine district education offices (PPD) in Selangor, Pahang, Sabah and Sarawak will also be shut. They are Hulu Langat and Sepang in Selangor; Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin in Pahang; Tawau in Sabah; and Serian, Sri Aman and Lubok Antu in Sarawak.
Today’s closures covered Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan and Putrajaya, along with the Hulu Langat, Petaling Perdana, Kuala Langat and Sepang PPDs in Selangor and the Kuantan and Rompin PPDs in Pahang. Pekan and the Sabah and Sarawak districts were not on that list.
During the closure, all pupils, including those in hostels, will follow Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) so that learning continues, in line with the ministry’s directive.
Parents and guardians were urged to make sure their children take part in PdPR.
The extension comes even though air quality in the state has eased.
According to Department of Environment (DOE) data as of 10.40am today, Seremban's API fell from 167 yesterday afternoon to 154, while Nilai dropped from 164 to 151. Port Dickson, which logged 154 yesterday, was no longer in the unhealthy range. An API reading of 101 to 200 is classed as unhealthy.
Nationwide, 20 of the 68 monitoring stations recorded unhealthy readings this morning, down from 23 yesterday.
Johor remained the worst affected, with eight unhealthy stations. Pasir Gudang recorded the highest reading in the country at 181, up from 174, followed by Larkin at 176 and Sri Aman in Sarawak at 170. No station recorded very unhealthy or hazardous levels.
Health and education authorities have advised parents, high-risk groups and students with respiratory ailments to wear face masks outdoors and to follow API updates through official channels.

Title: Zahid: Malaysia and China ramp up fight against cyber scams, cross-border crime
Article:
BEIJING, Oct 13 — Cross-border investigations and the recovery of assets stolen through cyber scams are among Malaysia’s key priorities in strengthening security cooperation with China, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said closer bilateral cooperation would help both countries tackle transnational crimes while delivering practical benefits under their comprehensive strategic partnership, particularly in security and law enforcement.
“We face several challenges in dealing with cyber scams, as the victims are not limited to Chinese nationals.
“That is why I believe bilateral cooperation between our countries is crucial in addressing this problem,” he told Malaysian media at a press conference here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, is on a five-day working visit to Beijing and Tianjin, which began yesterday.
The Deputy Prime Minister said Malaysia and China were also strengthening intelligence sharing and coordinating investigations and enforcement operations to combat cross-border crime.
Both countries had established a joint security committee, which also focuses on combating drug smuggling.
“Besides intelligence sharing and enforcement, we are adopting new methods to obtain early information on drug smuggling operations and facilities used to process illicit drugs.
“These efforts are already under way and will be further strengthened,” he said, adding that cooperation between Malaysian police and China’s National Narcotics Control Commission remained close.
Ahmad Zahid said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had held several discussions with his Chinese counterpart on the matter.
He said Malaysia, through the Drug Prevention Committee which he chairs, recognised the need for cross-border cooperation, with both countries making good progress in their efforts.
On cyber scams, Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia joined a programme under the International Alliance Against Telecommunications and Cyber Fraud on Sept 10, with cross-border investigations and stolen asset recovery identified as priorities.
“To strengthen the legal framework against cybercrime, I personally tabled the Cybercrime Bill in the Dewan Rakyat during the parliamentary sitting last July,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia: Super El Nino forecast for March-May 2027, temperatures could break Malaysia’s 40.1°C record
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 13 — Malaysia needs to brace itself for the Super El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to bring scorching weather between March and May next year, potentially breaking the country’s record high temperature of 40.1 degrees Celsius.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the country’s maximum temperature could exceed 41 degrees Celsius, based on analysis of the current intense El Niño phenomenon, alongside the impacts of climate change and global warming.
“If we look at current climate change trends, the rate of temperature increase in the country is approximately 0.13 degrees Celsius per decade.
“It has been nearly 30 years since 1998, when combined with the temperature spikes associated with El Niño, the increase could exceed one degree Celsius above the 40.1-degree record set back then. We anticipate that temperatures reaching 41 degrees Celsius or higher are likely to occur. That is our projection,” he said.
He made these remarks at a press conference following the National Climate Forum 2026 at Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) here today. The forum, themed “Preparedness Today, Resilience Tomorrow,” was attended by over 500 participants from various government departments and ministries.
Malaysia previously recorded its highest-ever temperature of 40.1 degrees Celsius in Chuping, Perlis, on April 9, 1998, during the 1997/1998 El Niño episode, while the peak temperature during the 2015/2016 episode was 39.3 degrees Celsius, recorded in Batu Embun, Pahang, on April 10, 2016.
Mohd Hisham said the current El Niño is projected to record an index exceeding 2.5, surpassing the peak level of 2.3 recorded during the 1997/1998 and 2015/2016 episodes.
He noted that during strong El Niño events, daily maximum temperatures can rise by up to 0.7 degrees Celsius above normal, while temperatures exceeding 35 degrees Celsius are expected to occur more widely and for longer periods.
Mohd Hisham added that the previously recorded scenario of up to 77 consecutive days without rain could recur particularly in the northern states of the Peninsula due to this El Niño phenomenon.
“Previous records show that this condition can begin at the end of the year, with a lack of rainfall starting in December and continuing through January and February, before rain returns around March,” he said.
In this regard, he emphasised that the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon currently forecast to begin in late October is crucial for ensuring dams receive sufficient rainfall and water storage levels are boosted before the country faces drier weather next year.
“We must ensure all our dams are full before next year begins. In terms of water sources, the Northeast Monsoon brings significant rainfall, and we hope this rain will fill all the dams,” he said.
He said this measure aligns with the directive from Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr. Ahmad Zahid Hamidi to make early preparations regarding water supply and storage in anticipation of the hot and dry spell next year.
Mohd Hisham also expressed concern regarding the anticipated rise in electricity consumption during next year’s hot weather, particularly due to the expected increase in air conditioner usage.
“Energy consumption will be high during the hot months next year. Therefore, regarding the energy grid, we must ensure there is sufficient capacity. A lack of preparedness could lead to disruptions and compromise the grid,” he said.
He said MetMalaysia has informed relevant agencies of this forecast, and the matter will be raised at the Disaster Management Council meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim next week.
At the same time, he noted that MetMalaysia is collaborating with the Ministry of Health (MOH) to develop a Heat Index. This will establish threshold values used to warn the public about health risks associated with hot weather.
He explained that the current hot weather monitoring system classifies temperatures of 35 degrees Celsius and above as Level 1, 37 degrees Celsius and above as Level 2, and 40 degrees Celsius and above as Level 3. — Bernama

Title: Asyraf says BN’s Melaka seat talks 90pc complete, urges trust in Muslim political pact
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is in the final stages of seat negotiations for the Melaka state election, with the coalition aiming to defend the 21 state constituencies it secured in the previous polls.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the remaining deliberations focus on the seven remaining seats across the 28-seat state legislative assembly, with potential seat swaps actively under consideration,
NST
reported.
“The negotiations have reached 90 per cent completion, with only 10 per cent remaining. In other words, we have agreed on the basic framework.
“There are seven more seats that we will discuss, including the possibility of seat swaps.
“We cannot deny the grassroots’ desire to see ‘perpaduan ummah’, particularly between the two largest Malay political parties, become a reality,” he told reporters after officiating the closing of the 2026 MRSM Bintang Media programme today.
While Asyraf declined to openly disclose the negotiating partners pending final agreement, his comments directly addressed the discussions between Umno and PAS.
Asked whether current talks appeared to lean favourably towards PAS, Asyraf cautioned that any working electoral pact must be anchored in mutual sincerity and trust.
“If we are friends, we must be genuine friends. Do not befriend someone only to stab them in the back.
“Do not appear friendly in front of them while intimidating them behind their backs through various means that are unbecoming of partners,” he said.
His remarks follow statements on Oct 2 by PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man, who said that electoral discussions between the two parties for the Melaka state election were in the final phase, having reached 90 per cent consensus.
The Election Commission (EC) has fixed Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka state election, with nominations to take place on Oct 31.

Title: Lorry driver in Shah Alam 12-vehicle pile-up pleads not guilty to drug-impaired driving
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 13 — A lorry driver pleaded not guilty in the Magistrates’ Court here to driving against traffic under the influence of drugs and causing injuries to four other individuals last week.
C. Agilan, 51, entered the plea after the charge against him was read out before Magistrate Ameera Mastura Khamis.
Agilan is accused of driving a lorry under the influence of methamphetamine and amphetamine, rendering him unable to control the vehicle and resulting in injuries to four individuals aged between 58 and 17. The offence was allegedly committed at about 4.30pm on October 9 at Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari.
He was charged under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which provides for a maximum jail term of 10 years and a maximum fine of RM50,000.
Deputy public prosecutor (DPP) Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan offered bail of RM15,000 and applied for the surrender of the accused’s driving licence.
Agilan’s lawyer Rohan Singh requested a minimum bail, citing that his client has to support his wife, who does not work, and an 11-year-old child on a salary of about RM1,700 a month.
Meanwhile, in a separate court before Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin, Agilan pleaded not guilty to a charge of self-administering methamphetamine and amphetamine at the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division office, Section 11, at about 11.30pm on October 9.
The charge was framed under Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which carries a jail term of up to two years, or a fine of up to RM5,000, upon conviction.
DPP Nur Amirah Zahari proposed bail of RM7,000, after which Rohan requested a minimum bail amount.
For the first charge, the court granted bail of RM9,000 and suspended his driving licence until the case is concluded, while for the second one, he was allowed bail of RM3,900.
The cases were set for mention on December 22 this year and January 11, 2027, respectively.
It was previously reported that four individuals were injured, one of them seriously, after a 10-tonne lorry driven against the flow of traffic crashed into 11 vehicles at the Alam Budiman traffic lights on Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari last week. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia cautious over proposal to co-chair The Hague Group, says Tok Mat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Malaysia must carefully consider a proposal by several countries for it to co-chair The Hague Group alongside South Africa, given legal constraints and its status as a non-party to relevant international conventions, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said accepting the role would raise questions about Malaysia’s participation in international legal instruments, including the Rome Statute, which he said could potentially conflict with the Federal Constitution.
He said the proposal followed Malaysia’s active involvement in the group, an international platform aimed at increasing pressure on Israel over the Palestinian issue.
“We must consider this carefully because Malaysia is not a state party to the convention. Therefore, we cannot become a co-chair.
“For now, it is sufficient for Malaysia to remain a co-sponsor and principal sponsor,” he said during Minister’s Question Time in reply to Datuk Muhammad Bakhtiar Wan Chik (PH-Balik Pulau) on Malaysia’s efforts to increase international pressure on Israel over the Palestinian conflict.
Mohamad said Malaysia had also joined South Africa as a co-sponsor at the recent United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) to intensify pressure on Israel, including efforts to bring the matter before the UN Security Council (UNSC).
He also noted that international support for the Palestinian cause was growing, including among countries that previously maintained close ties with Israel.
He said about 160 countries now supported Palestine’s admission as a UN member, reflecting a shift in international attitudes towards the issue.
Malaysia, he stressed, remained steadfast in defending Palestinian rights and continued to raise the issue through the UN, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), Asean and other multilateral platforms.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also consistently raised the Palestinian issue in meetings with world leaders and at international forums, including BRICS and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec).
Meanwhile, Mohamad reiterated Malaysia’s call for UNSC reform, particularly restrictions on the use of veto power, which he described as an obstacle to resolving the Palestinian conflict.
He said majority support for Palestine-related resolutions would achieve little if permanent UNSC members continued to block them through their veto powers.
“We need to restructure the UNSC so that veto power cannot be used arbitrarily,” he said.
On humanitarian assistance, Mohamad said contributions from Malaysians through the Foreign Ministry’s Palestinian Humanitarian Trust Account were channelled to the Palestinians through trusted organisations.
These included the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) and non-governmental organisations to ensure aid reached those in need, he added. — Bernama

Title: BYD driver still hospitalised as probe into fatal Jalan Kuching crash involving five-year-old girl heads to DPP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The driver of a BYD Seal involved in a six-vehicle collision that killed a five-year-old girl on Jalan Kuching is still receiving treatment at a private hospital.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said investigations into the incident were ongoing, Kosmo! Online reported today.
He said the investigating officer was working to complete the probe while continuing to monitor the driver’s condition.
“Investigations are ongoing. The driver is still receiving treatment at a private hospital and the investigating officer is completing the investigation and monitoring the driver’s condition.
“The case will be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) as soon as possible for further instructions. Any developments will be announced,” he said in a statement today.
It was  previously reported that the family of Asiah Ahmad Syahir, who died in the crash, would wait for the driver’s treatment and the police investigation to be completed before deciding on their next steps in seeking justice for the girl.
The victim’s 25-year-old uncle, Muhammad Amin Mohamad Nor Izam, said the family was leaving the investigation entirely to the police.
Asiah was pronounced dead from severe head injuries while being taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital following the collision at about 3.44pm.
Preliminary police investigations found that the Perodua Bezza carrying Asiah and her family was struck from behind by a BYD Seal.
The Bezza then spun into the right lane and collided with three other vehicles.

Title: Zara Qairina’s mother refused post-mortem despite being briefed, wanted immediate burial, inquest told
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 13 — The mother of Zara Qairina Mahathir, Noraidah Lamat, did not want a post-mortem conducted on her daughter and refused to allow it, despite being briefed on the matter, the Coroner’s Court was told today.
Investigating officer Insp Wong Yew Zhung said he had informed and explained to Noraidah, 46, at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital that a post-mortem would be conducted to assist investigations into Zara Qairina’s death.
The 83rd witness in the inquest proceedings into the teenager’s death explained the post-mortem process to Noraidah once again, but she remained adamant, replying: “I don’t want it. I want to bury her (Zara Qairina) immediately.”
Wong said a photographer took several photographs during the meeting and at the hospital’s Neurosurgery ward for record and documentation purposes.
“At that time, because Zara Qairina’s mother refused to allow a post-mortem to be conducted, and the cause of death had also been identified, no POL 61 form (document for a police application to conduct a post-mortem) was issued,” he said while reading his witness statement before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
Wong said Noraidah signed several documents on July 17, 2025, before Zara Qairina’s remains were handed over to the family for burial.
He said one document was a Letter of Declaration Refusing a Post-Mortem on One’s Own Volition, declaring that she did not want a post-mortem conducted, that she did not suspect any criminal act over the death, and that she would not demand any post-mortem report from the hospital for ‘medico-legal’ purposes, insurance claims, or other claims.
Wong said Noraidah also signed a Death Notification and Remains Handling Form, as acknowledgement of receipt of the remains, and a Letter of Declaration Confirming the Management of Remains Services on July 17, 2025.
“After meeting Zara’s mother, I returned to my office to update the case. I arrived at my office at IPD Papar at 6.54pm and received instructions to classify Zara’s death as a Sudden Death Report and to serve as the investigating officer in the probe,” he said.
Wong said he received a phone call from a doctor at 1.35pm on July 17, 2025, informing him that Zara Qairina had been pronounced dead at 1.07pm and that the student’s cause of death was “severe traumatic brain injury with hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy.”
He rushed to the hospital with the duty photographer, arrived at the hospital at 3.30pm, and met a doctor beside Zara Qairina’s bed, where Noraidah was also present.
Zara Qairina died at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after she was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel at 4am.
The inquest resumes later this afternoon. — Bernama
